newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks hold modest gains at close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks hold modest gains at close.

text.p: SPI futures 2430 +11 US 30yr cl 6.73 -0.01
10yrbond futs 92.295 +0.065 Gold NY 361.00 Lon fix 364.30
*Stocks end with modest gains after Dow rebounds, golds limit strength. Volume 332.61 million, value A$506.61 million, 1,082 stocks traded, 317 steady, 389 rises, 376 falls
The Australian share market ended with modest gains on Monday with a rebounding Wall Street providing the inspiration.
However, early strength was sapped by a gold sector that dived 1.6 percent after the bullion price tumbled offshore.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.3 points higher at 2,409.8. March share price index futures were up 11 points at 2,430, a 20.2 point premium to the index.
The bourse peaked early before CRA and WMC pulled it off its highs and by mid-morning it had found the four point range in which it spent most of the day.
"It's been running on the back of New York and it is still relatively quiet," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
A larger than expected November current account deficit passed barely noticed.
"The balance of payments did nothing for our market," Struk said.
With a dearth of corporate news on the leaders, the medium size oil companies took centre stage with a combination of value seeking investors and promising drilling results piquing trader's interest.

Featuring early was First Australian Resources whose shares shot up after it reported strong oil and gas flows from its south Louisiana field in the U.S. Its shares closed 44 percent higher at A$0.375.
Bligh Oil was also boosted by a U.S. drilling report from its first well in the Rainosek project in Texas, its shares ending up 28 percent at A$0.77.

Brokers cited investors looking for a competitively-priced entry to a buoyant energy sector for the strength of Cultus Petroleum, whose shares rose eight cents to A$1.38, and Tap Oil, whose shares rose six cents to A$0.93.
Situation stock Highlands Gold went against the gold sector trend, its shares adding four cents to A$0.79 after it unveiled restructuring plans to fend off a hostile bid from gold major Placer Dome.
In the industrials, shares in retailer David Jones continued to slide after Friday's warning of a 50 percent cut in first half net profit because of depressed retail trading conditions.
Shares in the upmarket department operator closed seven percent lower at A$1.56.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
The Australian dollar cowered close to the floor of a month-old range Monday as bearish chart forces combined with poor current account data to keep trade subdued.
Repeated failures at US$0.7985 resistance last week and resulting sales by frustrated U.S. funds had dragged the dollar to 79 cents late Friday and that was where it remained today.

Sentiment was further soured by an unexpected widening in the country's trade deficit, reflecting a slackening in commodity export earnings. By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) the local currency was pinned at US$0.7900/05 having slowly sagged from an early US$0.7905/10 and US$0.7915/20 late here Friday.
